title: Prorated quota banking and intra-month transfer for reserved capacity plan changes
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Problem: Customers on Reserved capacity occasionally change commit tiers mid-billing-cycle (upgrades, downgrades, or plan migrations). Current behavior: immediate rebilling or blunt resets cause either over-charging or dropped usable quota, and manual support interventions. Goal: implement a system that 'banks' unused quota proportionally (prorated) and allows intra-month transfer of remaining quota between plans or tenants under the same org, while preserving strict accounting for billing and auditability.
design_notes: Introduce a 'quota_bank' ledger per tenant that records credited token-seconds and debits at consume time. The bank balance is a monetary-unit equivalent stored in cents-per-token precision and anchored to billing_cycle_start.

On plan downgrade: compute prorated credit for remaining reserved capacity days, push into quota_bank as 'credit' with reason 'downgrade_proration' and metadata: previous_plan, new_plan, effective_date.
On plan upgrade: allocate immediate additional capacity subject to available pool; if pre-paid, debit quota_bank; otherwise schedule post-invoice adjustments.

Support intra-org transfer: allow admin API to move portion of quota_bank balance between tenants (audit-only if cross-billing-account). Transfer operations require two-step confirmation and are logged to audit-trail with UUID and operator id.
Accounting and billing: ledger entries are immutable. A reconciliation job runs daily to materialize token consumption into invoice line-items and consumes quota_bank credits FIFO by entry time.

Edge cases: tenants that revert changes within a 24-hour cooling window should be auto-reconciled to avoid churn; extremely large transfers (>50% of bank) trigger manual approval flag for finance review.
Migration: a one-time backfill to convert current 'remaining_quota' numeric to ledger entries; run under maintenance window with read-only requests for quota-affecting ops.
Data model note: quota_bank is a new table (ledger rows) but service layer exposes flat API methods. To keep this ticket schema-friendly, implementation details are in the linked design doc.

Performance: debit path must remain sub-millisecond for hot tenants; we'll implement in-memory cache with async durable write and circuit-breaker on DB contention. Kv-cache integration considered to avoid extra RPCs.

Privacy/compliance: ledger entries include no plaintext payment card data; only invoice ids and billing account ids. Retention policy aligns with billing retention (7 years) and is configurable by enterprise plans.

Trade-offs considered: Simpler approach of 'single-shot' prorate refunds rejected because it required finance refunds and increased latency for customers. Banking approach increases service complexity but keeps app-visible quota semantics immediate and predictable.
acceptance_criteria: On plan downgrade mid-cycle, customers see prorated credit applied to quota_bank and reduce next invoice by the computed amount (simulated in staging).
Quota consumption prefers quota_bank credits FIFO before charged usage, verified end-to-end with integration test and e2e accounting report matching expected invoice line-items.
Admin API for intra-org transfer exists with two-step confirmation and audit entries; unit tests and integration tests included.
Migration tool successfully backfills 95% of active tenants in staging with <10s downtime for quota writes and full reconciliation run completes within maintenance window target.
End-to-end latency for token consume path remains under 10ms p50 and p95 below 40ms for hot tenants after optimistic caching enabled.
Monitoring dashboards show quota_bank inflows/outflows, failed ledger writes, and reconciliation delta metrics; alerts fire on >0.25% reconciliation mismatch.
Finance sample invoices for 10 test tenants reflect prorated credits and no double-billing edge cases.
Security review signoff obtained if sensitive finance behavior changes are detected during implementation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Implement ledger schema, debit/credit APIs, and local reconciliation job. Run integration tests with synthetic tenants. (2 weeks).

Phase 2 (canary): Enable quota_bank for 5% of upgraded tenants on a dedicated reserved pool; expose 'experimental' flag in console for finance/SE to opt-in. Monitor metrics for errors and latency (1 week).
Phase 3 (gradual): Roll to 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 3 weeks with daily reconciliation checks and quick rollback doc. Support on-call rota notified for push windows.

Phase 4 (migration): Run one-time backfill for legacy remaining_quota into ledger. Provide support scheduler and run during low-traffic window. Post-migration, decommission legacy field after 30 days of zero reads.
Rollout safety: If reconciliation mismatch >0.5% for 24h, pause rollout and revert canary toggle. Provide manual adjustment endpoints for finance to correct ledger entries with audit trail.
Communication: Update Console billing UI to show 'banked credits' with explanation tooltips and link to docs. Notify active customers in advance for any maintenance windows.
GH PRs: split into schema + API + console + migration PRs to ease review. Each PR must include a small smoke DAG for nightly integration tests.
Post-release: 30-day runbook and ES playbook summarizing common failure modes and remediation steps.
Owner: Leah Ortiz; Backup owner: Priya Desai.
Rollback: API toggle to treat banked credits as disabled and fallback to legacy behavior for 48 hours.
monitoring_and_metrics: Daily reconciliation delta (expected invoiced vs materialized) metric with percent and absolute token delta
Ledger write error rate and latency histogram
Token consumption latency p50/p95 with and without bank cache
Number of intra-org transfer attempts, approvals, and failures
Number of manual ledger adjustments performed by finance
Alert: Ledger write failure rate >0.1% sustained for 10 minutes
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger debit/credit correctness including edge rounding cases
Integration tests simulating plan upgrade/downgrade sequences across billing cycles
E2E test that consumes tokens and validates invoice line-items generated by reconciliation job
Load test for debit path with cached bank balance to ensure <40ms p95 at 1k rps per shard
Migration dry-run: run backfill on a subset of historical data and validate idempotency
Security review and threat model test focusing on transfer API authorization and audit logging
Chaos test: simulate DB outage during reconciliation and ensure safe retries and idempotency
